meta.titre: Missionary Activity in Cameroon: Baptists, Basel, Catholics and their legacy
meta.sous_theme: Early missions, the founding of Victoria, and the impact of missionary work

sections.contenu_markdown: A church, a mission school or a hospital run by a church can be found in most Cameroonian towns. Many of these institutions have roots in the work of missionaries who arrived on the coast in the nineteenth century, before the colonial powers took control. Examiners ask about the first mission, about the founding of Victoria and about the effects of missionary work on education, health and society. This course puts the names and dates in order and shows you how to write a balanced answer.

items: A missionary is a person sent by a church to spread a religion.
Victoria is the old name of the town now called Limbe, at the foot of Mount Cameroon.
Cameroon was a German colony from 1884 until the First World War.

sections.titre: Missions in Cameroon: pioneers, Victoria and impact
sections.contenu_markdown:
### The pioneers

| Mission | Origin | Key facts |
|---|---|---|
| Baptist Missionary Society | Britain | The first mission body to set up stations on the Cameroon coast, from the 1840s. Joseph Merrick, a Jamaican Baptist, worked at Bimbia and Alfred Saker, an English Baptist, worked at Douala |
| Basel Mission | Switzerland and Germany | Took over much of the Baptist work after the German annexation, in the mid-1880s |
| Pallottine Fathers | Germany (Catholic) | The first Catholic missionaries, who arrived in 1890 |
| American Presbyterians | United States | Worked mainly in the south of the territory |

### Victoria and Buea

In 1858 Alfred Saker founded Victoria on Ambas Bay as a Christian settlement, named after Queen Victoria. Among the first settlers were Christians who had left Fernando Po after Spain restricted Protestant worship there. Victoria became a Baptist centre. After the German takeover, the Germans needed a healthier site for their capital. Early in the twentieth century they chose Buea, on the slopes of Mount Cameroon, because its cooler climate was healthier for Europeans. Governor Jesko von Puttkamer was in office at the time.

### Impact of the missions

| Area | What the missions did |
|---|---|
| Education | Opened schools that taught reading, writing and arithmetic and trained teachers and clerks |
| Language | Saker translated the Bible into Duala, and missions printed books in African languages |
| Health | Opened dispensaries and hospitals |
| Society | Opposed slavery and sheltered freed people; produced an educated group of pastors, teachers and clerks |

### Criticisms

Some missionaries condemned African customs they did not understand. Missions often worked inside the colonial system and depended on the goodwill of the authorities. Their schools reached only a part of the population.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks which mission, who, when or where
variantes.contenu_markdown: Give the name and the place together. First mission: the Baptist Missionary Society. Victoria: founded in 1858 by Alfred Saker. Capital moved to Buea: for a healthier climate. Catholics: the Pallottine Fathers in 1890.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks for the effects of missionary work
variantes.contenu_markdown: Take each effect (education, health, language, society) as a point and add a result: schools produced teachers and clerks, hospitals reduced suffering, written languages preserved local culture. Add one limit to show balance.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks whether missionaries helped colonisation
variantes.contenu_markdown: Argue both sides. For: they arrived before the annexation, taught the colonial language in some schools and worked within the authorities' rules. Against: they criticised abuses and used African languages, and they were not part of the government. Judge in a final sentence.

sections.enonce_markdown: Discuss the contribution of Christian missions to the development of education in Cameroon before 1914. [10 marks]

etapes.action: Read the command word 'Discuss' and the limits.
etapes.justification: 'Discuss' needs two sides. The limits are education only and the period before 1914.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Plan: the contributions, the limits, then a judgement.

etapes.justification: Missions arrived decades before the colonial government and opened schools first.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Baptist missionaries opened schools on the coast from the mid-nineteenth century and taught reading, writing and arithmetic.

etapes.justification: Written language is a key tool of education.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Missions printed books in African languages, and Saker translated the Bible into Duala.

etapes.justification: Schools produced people who later worked in the colonial economy and in the church.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Pupils became teachers, clerks, interpreters and pastors.

etapes.justification: A balanced answer shows the weaknesses of the system.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Schools reached only a small part of the population, and their first purpose was religious teaching.

etapes.justification: The judgement answers 'discuss' with a clear view.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Missions laid the foundation of education in Cameroon, although the system was small.

sections.conclusion_markdown: Model answer: Christian missions made a major contribution to education in Cameroon before 1914, although their reach was small. The Baptist missionaries, who arrived in the 1840s, opened the first schools on the coast and taught reading, writing and arithmetic. They also gave written form to African languages: Alfred Saker translated the Bible into Duala, and missions printed books in local languages. Their schools trained teachers, clerks, interpreters and pastors, who were needed by the churches and by the colonial economy. However, schools reached only a small part of the population, and the main purpose was religious teaching. In conclusion, the missions laid the foundation of education in Cameroon, even if the system remained limited.

items.erreur_markdown: "The first missionaries in Cameroon were Catholic."
items.pourquoi_faux: The first mission on the coast was Protestant, run by the Baptist Missionary Society. Catholic Pallottine missionaries came in 1890.
items.correction_markdown: Write: Baptist Missionary Society first; Catholic Pallottines in 1890.

items.pourquoi_faux: Saker was an English Baptist. The Germans came after the annexation of 1884.
items.correction_markdown: Write: Alfred Saker, English Baptist missionary, founder of Victoria in 1858.

items.erreur_markdown: "Missionaries came to Cameroon after the Germans and helped them to annex it."
items.pourquoi_faux: The first missionaries arrived in the 1840s, about forty years before the German annexation.
items.correction_markdown: Say that the missions arrived before the colonial period and later worked within the German system.

items.erreur_markdown: "Victoria was the capital of German Kamerun."
items.pourquoi_faux: Victoria was a mission and port settlement. The German capital was moved to Buea, which has a cooler climate.
items.correction_markdown: Write: Victoria, Baptist settlement of 1858; Buea, German capital chosen for its climate.

items.erreur_markdown: In a ten-mark question a student only lists the names of the missions.
items.pourquoi_faux: A list of names does not explain the impact of the missions, so most marks are lost.
items.correction_markdown: Add what each mission did and what the result was.

items.enonce_markdown: State **two** services, other than preaching, that early missionaries provided to Cameroonians.
items.solution_markdown:
Possible answers: **education** (schools), **health care** (dispensaries and hospitals), **translation and printing of books** in African languages, and **shelter for freed people**.

Award one mark for each valid service, up to **2 marks**.

items.enonce_markdown: Explain **two** ways in which missionary work prepared some Cameroonians for later work in the colonial administration. [4 marks]
items.solution_markdown:
Way 1: mission schools taught reading, writing and arithmetic, skills needed for clerical work. Way 2: the schools trained interpreters and teachers who could work between the foreign officials and the local people.

Award one mark for each way and one for its explanation. Total: **4 marks**.

items.enonce_markdown: To what extent were missionaries agents of colonial rule in Cameroon? [10 marks]
items.solution_markdown:
For the view: missions arrived before the annexation, some taught the language of the colonial power, depended on the authorities for protection, and their schools produced the clerks the administration needed. Against the view: missions had their own religious aims, they used African languages, they opposed slavery and some abuses, and they were not part of the government. Judgement: missionaries were not simple agents of the colonial state, but their work helped and was helped by colonial rule.

Award marks for knowledge (4), balance (4) and judgement (2). Final answer: **partly, but they had aims of their own**.

items_markdown: The Baptist Missionary Society was the first mission body on the coast, from the 1840s; Merrick worked at Bimbia and Saker at Douala.
Alfred Saker founded Victoria in 1858 as a Christian settlement, named after the queen.
The Germans later chose Buea as capital because of its cooler, healthier climate.
The Basel Mission took over much of the Baptist work after 1884, and the Catholic Pallottine Fathers arrived in 1890.
The missions gave Cameroon schools, hospitals, written African languages and a first educated class.
For a balanced answer, add the limits: small reach, religious aims and work within colonial rule.
